chats.answer:
The Keychron K5 Max is my best overall pick for a full-size, low-profile mechanical keyboard with a number pad. It has a traditional 100% layout, comfortable low-profile switches, wireless connectivity, and excellent customization without the premium price of most gaming keyboards. I'd choose Brown tactile switches for typing and spreadsheets, or Red linear switches for a smoother keypress. 
RTINGS.com

Best full-size low-profile mechanical keyboards

All three picks below have a separate number pad, function row, arrow keys, and navigation cluster. I've prioritized a traditional full-size layout rather than compact keyboards that squeeze in a numpad.

Best overall and best value

Keychron K5 Max

$86.24

Keychron

108 keys, 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth for three devices, USB-C, and programmable keys. Choose the hot-swappable version if you want to change switches. Main drawback: the stock key legends don't illuminate. 
RTINGS.com

Best premium gaming keyboard

Logitech G915 X LIGHTSPEED — Linear

$159.99

newegg.com

Excellent wireless latency, illuminated PBT keycaps, dedicated media controls, and a volume roller. Better for gaming in a dark room, but more expensive and less customizable than the Keychron. 
RTINGS.com

Best ultra-thin, laptop-like feel

Corsair K100 AIR Wireless — Tactile

$401.61

Best Buy

Just 11mm thick at its thinnest point, with ultra-low-profile mechanical switches, short travel, and crisp tactile feedback. The strongest choice if minimum height matters more than price. 
RTINGS.com

What I'd buy: the K5 Max with Brown switches and the hot-swappable PCB. It offers the best balance for everyday typing, number-pad work, and occasional gaming. The main reason I'd spend more is to get the Logitech's shine-through legends and dedicated controls.

I assumed you want a conventional US full-size layout and haven't set a budget. Prices are retailer listings, not guaranteed checkout prices; verify the switch and hot-swap configuration before ordering.

chats.answer:
I'd buy the Keychron K5 Ultra 8K. It has a true full-size layout with a separate number pad, navigation cluster and arrow keys, plus low-profile mechanical switches. It's my best all-around pick if you want a slim keyboard for typing, spreadsheets and occasional gaming.

Best full-size low-profile mechanical keyboards

Keychron K5 Ultra 8K

$103.49

Keychron

Best overall. Hot-swappable low-profile switches, programmable keys, volume knob, Bluetooth, 2.4GHz wireless and USB. Up to 8,000Hz polling for gaming. A strong feature set for the money. 
Technobezz

Keychron K5 Max

$86.24

Keychron

Best independently tested pick. Smooth, pre-lubricated switches and excellent wireless performance. Choose Brown for tactile feedback or Red for a smooth press. Stock keycap legends don't illuminate; hot-swap is optional. 
RTINGS.com

Logitech MX Mechanical — Tactile Quiet

$142.99

Walmart

Best for office work. Subdued styling, illuminated keys, quieter tactile switches and easy switching between three devices. Less customizable than the Keychron options.

Logitech G915 X LIGHTSPEED — Tactile

$159.99

newegg.com

Best premium gaming option. Excellent latency, durable PBT keycaps, RGB lighting, dedicated macro and media controls, and a volume roller. Wider and generally more expensive than the Keychrons. 
RTINGS.com

Which switch should you get? For general typing and number-pad work, I'd start with tactile Brown switches: you feel a small bump when pressing a key without the deliberate click of a clicky switch. Choose linear Red switches if you prefer a smooth, light keystroke.

I interpreted full size as a traditional 100% layout, not a compressed 96% keyboard that happens to include a numpad. I also assumed no particular budget or operating system. The Ultra is my feature-based recommendation; the Max has stronger independent testing behind it, and I haven't personally tested either. Check the selected switch variant and checkout price before ordering.
